Challenging judgment and award dated 12.05.2014 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge at Gadag (for short, 'Tribunal') in MVC no.376/2012, these appeals are filed.

sentences.text: 2. While MFA no.102536/2014 is filed by Insurer, MFA no.102060/2014 is by claimants.
3. Sri SK Kayakamath, learned counsel for appellant in MFA no.102536/2014 submitted that appeal was by insurer being aggrieved by finding of Tribunal on liability.

It was submitted as per claimants on 02.05.2012, Jaibunnabi along with others were travelling in Truck no.KA-25/C-1715 along with dry chilly bags from Gadag towards Udupi by sitting in cabin and by paying hire charges.

However,
when lorry was near Jadikatti Bridge, Mirjan village, it met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving by its driver.
In accident, Jaibunnabi and Gangavva Bhandivaddar died on spot.
Alleging loss of dependency on account of sudden demise, Jaibunnabi's husband and four major children filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act against insurer of Lorry.

4 opposed claim petition alleging that insured vehicle was a Goods Lorry and deceased along with others were travelling in it as gratuitous passengers and therefore insurer was not liable to pay compensation.
Claim petition was also opposed on various other grounds.
5. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Two witnesses were examined by claimants as PW1 and PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P8.
Respondent/Insurer examined its official as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, vehicle was duly insured and claimants were entitled for compensation of 4,85,500/- with interest at 6% per annum from owner and insurer jointly and severally.
Aggrieved, insurer was in appeal.
6. It was submitted at time of accident, Lorry in question was loaded with cement bags and there was no evidence led to establish that deceased were travelling in Lorry as owner of goods.
Only document sought to be relied upon NC: 2026:KHC-D:4919 HC-KAR namely Ex.P8, a receipt of purchase of chilly, but not pertaining to deceased.
Therefore, pleading that deceased were travelling in goods vehicle as owner or hirer of goods vehicle was only for purposes of claim.
It was submitted in cross examination, PW1 admitted that except Ex.P8, he had no other record to establish that his wife was carrying on sale of chilly.
Suggestion that she was unauthorized and gratuitous passenger in goods vehicle, was denied.
Such being case, Tribunal erred in fastening liability on insurer.
On said ground sought for allowing appeal.

7. On other hand, Sri Deepak C. Maganur, learned counsel appearing for respondents no.1 to 5/claimants opposed insurer's appeal and submitted that claimants had filed MFA no.102060/2014 for enhancement of compensation.
Insofar as insurer appeal, it was submitted that complaint was filed by one of inmates of Lorry, stating that deceased was travelling with chilly load for sale at Udupi.
Same duly corroborated claimants' pleadings.
Even Ex.P8 would corroborate same and therefore, there was no justification in insurer's appeal.

For enhancement, it was submitted that compensation of 5,000/- awarded towards funeral expenses was on lower side and NC:
2026:KHC-D:4919 HC-KAR sought for enhancement.
On said two grounds sought for allowing appeal.

8. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.
9.

From above, since both insurer as well as claimants are in appeal, points that would arise for consideration are,
(i) Whether Tribunal was justified in holding insurer liable to pay compensation?
( ii) Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?
10. Point no.(i) : From above, there is no dispute about occurrence of accident and involving insured vehicle leading to death of Jaibunnabi.
Specific contention of insurer is that Jaibunnabi was a gratuitous passenger as on date of accident and therefore, insurer would not be liable to pay Branch Manager vs Kumari.

5 compensation.
It is seen that claimants have specifically pleaded that deceased was travelling in vehicle as owner of goods and hirer of vehicle.

A perusal of complaint filed by one Hanumant son of Mudiappa Kavalur indicates that as on date of NC: 2026:KHC-D:4919 HC-KAR accident he was travelling in vehicle on instructions of Hanamanthgouda with whom he was working as an Assistant and was instructed to go to Mangalore and collect hire fare.
He stated that at Gadag, five people boarded vehicle to go to Udupi along with vegetables and chilly load.
Claimants also rely on Ex.P8-chilly purchase receipt to corroborate trade in chilly.
But Ex.P8 reveals that it was issued to some other person and not to any of passengers or deceased.
As such, Ex.P8 would not be of relevance.
However, as per complaint, complainant was travelling in vehicle on instructions of owner of vehicle to collect hire fare and he deposed that deceased was travelling in vehicle along with goods.
11. Ex.P3-spot panchanama mentions about chilly sacks being spread at accident spot.
Thus, there is some corroboration of claimant's assertion that deceased was travelling in goods vehicle along with goods for sale at Udupi.
On other hand, in cross-examination of PW1, only elicitations are about claimant having no other document than Ex.P8 to establish, deceased was trading in chilly.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:4919 HC-KAR 12.
While passing impugned award, Tribunal has referred to material on record and held deceased was travelling in goods vehicle as owner of goods.
Thus finding of Tribunal is based on material on record and cannot be held to be perverse.
Point no.(i) is answered in affirmative.
13. Point no.(ii) :
On quantum, though claimant stated that deceased was earning Rs.9,000/-, same was not established.
In absence, Tribunal rightly assessed it notionally.
Notional income for year 2012 is Rs.6,500/- and therefore same has to be considered.

While assessing compensation,
Tribunal deducted one fourth (1/4th) towards personal expenses, applied multiplier of '11', but Tribunal did not add future prospects.
Taking note of ratio in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi1 ('Pranay Sethi' for short), considering age of deceased at 51 years, 10% has to be added towards future prospects.
